title: Composite and inverse functions

points.text: Forming composite functions and reading the order correctly
Finding an inverse algebraically, including domain restrictions

bigPicture: Composite functions chain one rule into another; inverses undo a rule. Order matters: f∘g means do g first.

keyIdeas.answer: Write y = f(x), swap x and y, make y the subject; restrict domain so f is one-to-one.

keyTerms.def: function made by applying one function to the output of another
each output from only one input

misconceptions.right: Only one-to-one functions (possibly after restricting the domain).

practice.prompt: f(x) = 2x − 1, g(x) = x² + 3. Find (a) (g∘f)(x) (b) f⁻¹(x) (c) solve (f∘g)(x) = 13.
h(x) = e^(0.5x) + 1. Find h⁻¹(4) and verify on the GDC.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.

memorise: Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f
